Prior authorization is horrifying for someone with a chronic condition.

I have chronic spontaneous urticaria (fancy way to say hives all over for no reason) and one of the most effective treatments for me has been Xolair. It's a specialty medication, so normal pharmacies don't carry it and it has to be insurance approved and shipped to a doctor's office.

I was ultimately denied three times through appeal through three different insurance companies. We picked our insurance plans specifically because I require this medication, and still were denied. I've only been approved once and it's the only time I've had some small semblance of quality of life in the last 12 years.

It's abusive, it's inhumane, and it is costing lives.

comments.text: I have worked in medical billing for 14 years and also did hospital billing related to Medicare replacement plans. Those plans require an authorization for patients to be admitted to the hospital and most of my work was to appeal the inpatient claims they denied for no authorization. I saw so many cases where they didn’t consider the stay as medically necessary even after what’s called a “peer to peer review”, where the doctor who admitted the patient talks to the insurance doctor. What makes it worse is that even after that appeal, the patient would have to be sent home, and would come back hours later and pass away from the gap in care. Providers do often try to help with the appeals process but it’s very time consuming, so they often change the treatment plan instead. I really understand what they’re talking about in this video because I’ve seen it firsthand.
